public.prompt: A batch validator obtains `document.getElementsByClassName('pending')`. While an asynchronous validation loop runs, other code adds and removes matching elements. The batch must process exactly the elements present at capture time. Which boundary supplies that stable membership?

options.label: Keep the returned HTMLCollection and cache its initial length before iterating the numbered entries.
Keep the returned HTMLCollection and iterate it after each asynchronous validation has completed.
Copy the returned HTMLCollection with `Array.from` before starting any asynchronous validation work.

answerProof.summary: The class-name query returns a live HTMLCollection whose membership follows DOM changes; converting it to an Array creates the required point-in-time list.
decisiveConstraints: DOM membership may change while asynchronous work is pending.
The batch membership is fixed at capture time.
Each captured element must be processed once.

claims.statement: An HTMLCollection is live and updates as its underlying document changes.
Array.from creates a new Array from an iterable or array-like value.

optionRationales.explanation: Caching a length does not freeze which elements occupy the live collection's numbered entries.
optionRationales.plausibility: A fixed loop bound can appear to isolate iteration from later additions.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: Removals and insertions can shift the live entries even when the numeric bound stays fixed.

optionRationales.explanation: Reading the live collection after awaits observes later DOM membership instead of the original batch.
optionRationales.plausibility: Deferred iteration can ensure each element is checked against the latest rendered DOM.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: Elements added after capture must not join this validation batch.

optionRationales.explanation: Array.from materializes the current members into a separate array before asynchronous DOM changes occur.
